items.text: [p align="start"]The roads are about to get a lot louder. Arriving alongside the latest 1.9 Major Update, Arma Reforger Rally DLC brings a new single-player racing experience to the islands. Choose from three rally cars, take on six tracks, and put your driving skills to the test against the clock. With a major vehicle simulation overhaul arriving in the same update, there is plenty changing beneath the bonnet, too.
[dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/5146340/Arma_Reforger_Rally/"]

[p align="start"]This DLC brings six tracks across Everon, Arland, and Kolguyev, taking you through wooded bends, across the airfield, and down volcanic slopes. Roads you might normally cross on the way to an objective become a challenge of their own.

[p align="start"]Customizable race conditions give you more ways to test yourself. Learn the route, get a feel for the grip, and find the balance between speed and making it through the next corner. A little confidence can save you time. Too much... and you might meet a tree.

[p align="start"]Three rally cars bring different strengths and handling characteristics to the starting line. Each comes with a choice of racing liveries, but what is underneath will matter more for your finishing time. Vehicle access follows the approach used in Arma 3; where owners can drive DLC vehicles, while players who do not own the DLC can still ride in them as passengers.

[p align="start"]An upgraded 130-horsepower engine, a five-speed gearbox, and a wider body kit turn the familiar Šárka into a much more ambitious machine. With a racing steering wheel and other rally upgrades, this is a car ready to be pushed. Just make sure your braking points are ready, too.

[p align="start"]Lightweight, unconventional, and powered by a two-stroke engine, the Sputnik 600 RS is an East German classic that trades everyday duties for rally tuning, letting its compact body tackle corners at a very different speed.

[p align="start"]The Dana's recognizable Soviet styling, dashboard, and steering wheel remain, but its rally variant has a different job to do. Sitting between the Šárka and Sputnik, the Dana 2001 RS offers a balanced alternative as you work out which car best suits your driving style.
[p align="start"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42399725/ff4af909d8530f5820c4f2c6c618b546baa47f93.jpg"]
[p align="start"]Rally's single-player time trials give you a reason to return to each track. Chase ghost times, learn where you are gaining or losing seconds, and push to improve your own best run.

[p align="start"]Expect to spend some time learning. These cars reward practice, and your first attempts may involve more sliding, spinning, and rolling than you intended. If you end up on your roof, AI spectators can help put your car back on its wheels so you can keep going.
[p align="start"]Get comfortable with one car, try another, and see how much of what you learned carries over. There is always another run to make and another braking point to get right.
[p align="start"]Rally DLC arrives alongside a major vehicle simulation overhaul in the free 1.9 platform update. These driving improvements are available to everyone, regardless of DLC ownership.

[p align="start"]Engines, clutches, differentials, and wheels have been reworked, alongside changes to steering, tires, and suspension. Vehicles respond more realistically to the road, manual driving demands more clutch care, and vehicles with multiple driven axles benefit from improved torque distribution on uneven terrain.

[p align="start"]Support for racing wheels, pedals, and gear shifters, including force feedback, gives you more ways to drive. Mouse steering and more consistent steering speeds across input devices also improve the experience for keyboard and controller users. Dust, mud, skid marks, and tire smoke add to the action.
[p align="start"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42399725/90deb8c0679156179b41b98b4419af7df37c86aa.jpg"]
[p align="start"]Beyond driving, the 1.9 update includes several additions to everyday gameplay:
Foliage removal: Use a shovel to clear bushes and low foliage. Building bases and larger compositions also clears obstructing vegetation.
Magazine repacking: Combine ammunition from compatible magazines to make better use of the rounds you have left.
LAV-25 upgrades: A night vision optic, smoke launchers, and a rate-of-fire selector expand its capabilities. Its supply cost and rank requirement have increased accordingly.
Canteens: Replenish your hydration to support stamina and steadier aim while operating in the field.
[p align="start"]The update also brings further fixes and improvements across the game. Read the full 1.9 changelog for the complete breakdown.
[p align="start"]Pick your car, learn the track, and see how much time you can shave off your next run. Find out more about Arma Reforger Rally DLC on Steam.
We'll see you on the track!

The 1.8 Major Update is here, bringing new features, gameplay improvements, stability fixes, and plenty of changes across the battlefield. We're also excited to announce that Arma Reforger is now available on the Microsoft Store with Xbox Play Anywhere support, allowing you to play across Xbox consoles and Windows PC with a single digital purchase.

One of the biggest additions in 1.8 is the first iteration of our new Far Hide system, designed to address situations where players hiding in grass at long distances would leave you completely exposed to enemy snipers. Turns out, lying perfectly still in a field isn't much help when the field disappears.

Far Hide helps conceal distant characters against areas covered by grass, so lying in a field should no longer make you stick out like a sore thumb to someone watching from 750 meters away. There may still be some tweaks we would like to make as we continue developing this feature, but we hope this first implementation helps reduce the advantage players had from vegetation no longer rendering at longer distances or when lowering graphics settings.

Concealment is also becoming more important when fighting AI. Grass and camo nets can now obstruct AI vision, making vegetation and camouflage more useful for breaking line of sight. AI should have a harder time spotting and tracking players now.
Your role within a squad now matters! In 1.8, several specialist roles gain advantages when performing job-related tasks, hopefully giving your Medic more purpose than before.

Medics can inspect and treat wounded soldiers faster and load casualties into vehicles. Logistics personnel can load and unload supplies faster, while vehicle crews can repair, rearm, and refuel vehicles more quickly. Engineers also receive faster construction speeds when building structures or deployables.

Speaking of building, field fortification has also received some quality-of-life improvements. You no longer need to throw an entire collection of sandbags onto the ground before constructing something (like sandbags). Having one available to begin deployment is enough, with the remaining required items taken directly from your inventory.

Players can also now deploy razor wire themselves, giving engineers another tool for blocking points or funneling infantry into more favorable ambushes. The PKMN can now be deployed on the 6T5 tripod, with or without the 1P29 optic.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42399725/21c4d3c5c249573cb11b31fc9e06e5655c66854e.jpg"]

We've added more options for communicating and coordinating without saying a word. New tactical gesture animations provide additional ways to communicate visually with teammates, as well as more casual loiter animations that give you something to do during the calm of battle. Sit down, do some pushups, or take a moment for a smoke before everything inevitably goes wrong again.

The US Army also receives underbarrel smoke grenades in several colors, giving grenadiers another way to screen movement or mark locations. Smoke mortar rounds have also been adjusted to remain effective for longer, making mortar-deployed smoke a more umore useful option for covering an assault, or at the very least making everyone less certain about what they're actually shooting at.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42399725/3bcfd57f9c56344ad5d73a2a5388e1e5f9309b56.jpg"]
There are plenty of other additions and improvements included with 1.8. Here are a few more worth highlighting:
Running around without boots can now damage your feet and carries a small chance of causing your character to stumble and fall. So maybe think twice before charging barefoot across Everon.

Dying now costs 30 rank progression points, giving you another reason to value your life beyond the long walk back from spawn. Deaths caused by friendly fire will not penalize the victim's rank progression, and dying will not cause a player to become a Renegade.
Admins can teleport their camera directly to players and promote or demote players through the Player List.
MOB construction is no longer prevented simply by the presence of nearby enemies. So being shot at is no longer considered a valid excuse to stop building.

And finally, as always, we've implemented an array of new crash fixes, memory and pathfinding improvements, VoN updates, and other optimizations. Not the flashiest part of an update, but your PC or console will probably appreciate it. Of course, we've introduced more fixes and optimizations than we could reasonably cover here, so if you want, you can read the full list in the 1.8 Update changelog.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42399725/faab93d1d8c82ef4115fff58bcc5b6015f63c05e.jpg"]
We hope you enjoy this set of new additions and improvements. Our work is not done, and we will continue releasing patches and updates over the coming weeks and months.

Features will continue to be refined, bugs will be fixed, and community feedback remains an important part of helping us identify issues and improve the game. Please report any feedback you might have through the Feedback Tracker.

Base capturing was previously set up for two factions, and it was necessary to rework it to provide better player feedback. A new state has been added: Contesting.
The core of capturing is still identical. Have more friendly characters in the capture zone than the opposing factions to start the process. The in-between state is what has changed.
If the defenders are outnumbered and no capture is occurring, the base will change to a "contested" state.
A capture can be prevented (and so contested will happen) due to
FIA (who is unable to capture entirely)
The factions fighting over the point being equal in number
Either of the major factions trying to capture without a radio connection
When a base is contested, defenders are unable to spawn on the base for as long as it remains contested. This is shown on the map with a soft red glow around the base.
Though this is a "nerf" to defenders for spawning, they now get more information to work with.
It should balance out for enemies being present in backline bases, as it shows you when bases are being messed with while still not allowing spawning on "hot" frontline bases.

[p align="start"]The FIA has become a playable third faction in Arma Reforger Conflict scenarios. Playing as FIA is not for the unprepared, though. You will be outnumbered, outgunned, thrown into the world with minimal equipment, and with no clear task ahead. How you choose to approach the conflicts of two world superpowers as an underequipped partisan is entirely up to you. It will not be an easy fight!

[p align="start"]The islands of Everon, Arland, and Kolguyev make up an unforgiving battlefield between the US and USSR armies, with you as a guerrilla in the middle. So, get yourself prepared for the battle ahead. You spawn with just a pistol, a spare magazine, and a "shopping list." It is a guide that will lead you to hidden equipment caches at random locations. Keep your shopping list with you and protect it. Should it fall into the hands of the enemy, you might just find an unwanted surprise at your next cache visit.
[p align="start"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42399725/d5b050d9196229f0131e7149079bdaeb75759189.jpg"]

[p align="start"]Hidden FIA equipment caches give you a wide selection of gear to prepare yourself. Uniforms, vests, weapons, ammunition, mines, medical items, crew weapons, and deployable tents. But as with everything in Arma Reforger Conflict, supplies are a vital resource that allows you to use whatever gear you need. Keep your hidden arsenals supplied for yourself and for your comrades whenever you can. Otherwise, you might need to rely on enemy bases for usable loot.
[p align="start"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42399725/d59ea84b2afbdc1602a125a0a5fe760bf825c6ab.jpg"]

[p align="start"]FIA spawns are randomized after the islands have been overrun by US and USSR troops. To make your cause easier for yourself, deploy secret hideouts using the tents obtainable from the hidden arsenal boxes. These hideouts let you spawn anywhere on the battlefield so long as you keep them stocked up on supplies. Hide them well; they might be your only way of keeping your friendlies together.
[p align="start"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42399725/e42d146bfb9c7fce2a66cb9ee59308c3ff0b5060.jpg"]

[p align="start"]For any US and USSR troops, traversing the warzones of Arma Reforger has just become a different challenge. From now on, you can never be sure if the FIA enemy manning a checkpoint on your way to the nearest objective is now a real player or not. Stay vigilant, don't get complacent, and stay in the fight!
[p align="start"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42399725/25afb5caa4a2f349331156eba42a659ed584e5a4.jpg"]

[p align="start"]Driving has been overhauled with adjustments to vehicle weights, suspension heights, torque, and other parameters to bring the final state to a more realistic standard. We understand this might be a divisive topic with various preferences. We plan to keep tweaking the vehicle simulation until we get it right. Feel free to leave your thoughts and experiences using our new Feedback Tracker.

[p align="start"]Reconnect Queue has been added to mitigate a previously prevalent "SERVER_FULL" issue. This occurred when players tried to join servers while others were reconnecting at the same time, costing them their allocated server slot. Now you might be placed in a new queue designed to avoid clashes between joining and reconnecting players. It is a separate queue from the main queue, and it may occur even when the player numbers haven't reached the maximum allowed number. The Reconnect Queue should not take longer than one or two minutes.
[p align="start"]Here are some other notable changes to gameplay:
Strafing inertia - Side-to-side character movement has been adjusted to mitigate "strafe spamming" in firefights.
Bush slowdown - Characters are no longer able to sprint through bushes as if they don't exist. Thick vegetation slows you down now.

Improved vehicle unflipping - Repair trucks parked near flipped vehicles reduce the number of players needed to unflip such a vehicle to one. This way, you can get your BTR, transport truck, or Buchanka back on the road all on your own.
Mod storage - Xbox players can now utilize up to 50 GB of storage space for mods on their consoles.
Mod uploads - Workbench uploads to the Workshop are now split into smaller chunks, improving uploads and significantly reducing errors.
Destructible razor wire - Players can now use bayonet-equipped rifles to destroy razor wire emplacements.
[p align="start"]There are many more changes, fixes, and optimizations in the 1.7 update. You can read the full list here: 1.7 Update changelog

[p align="start"]Some features and tweaks in 1.7 will continue to be adjusted in future updates. We are releasing 1.7 now to address many of the crashes introduced in 1.6 and to enable modders to more reliably upload their mods. We consider these improvements, along with many other changes in 1.7, significant enough to release this version to the main application.

[p align="start"]Our work is not done, and we will be releasing further patches and updates over the next weeks and months. Features will be refined, bugs will be fixed, and we always appreciate community feedback to help us identify issues. Please report any feedback you might have to the Feedback Tracker.
[p align="start"]We greatly appreciate your support and hope you enjoy the new version of Arma Reforger.

items.text: Starting today, the battle for Kolguyev has launched for all Arma Reforger players. Set foot on this harsh volcanic island and experience one of the largest updates to the game to date. In Update 1.6, take command in the drastically overhauled Conflict HQC game mode, experience the new Operation Omega singleplayer campaign and Air Support scenario, and gear up with new weapons, equipment, and systems to lead your team to victory.

Kolguyev has finally returned to the Armaverse, reimagined in the Enfusion engine. This rugged volcanic island contrasts beautifully with Everon’s lush greenery, trading grass fields for windswept pines, barren ridges, and the warm hues of the autumn season. Beneath its dormant volcano lies a network of steaming hot springs and winding sulfur streams. Scattered across the island are the rusted remains of an old coal industry.

The classic Conflict experience has been completely rebuilt into Headquarters Commander (HQC). In this new rendition of the game mode, a player can step into the role of Commander and coordinate the war effort by assigning tasks to player squads, managing AI logistic units, and leading their faction to victory.

Bases are no longer just fixed objectives but can now be constructed anywhere across an island. Players can also rise through the ranks by contributing to their squad’s success, such as staying close to squadmates, healing allies, repairing vehicles, and completing assigned objectives. Every squad features unique loadouts, group types, and roles designed to coordinate with the entire team.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42399725/addb79d12757cf15132af45a2943c649695bfad7.jpg"]

Resource management now plays a critical role, as the new supply scarcity system requires you to retrieve and transport materials from nearby harbors or depots to keep your forces operational. Don’t worry, though, players also have their own personal supply called Military Supply Allocation by Rank (MSAR), so they aren’t draining all the team's supplies at the arsenal. HQC represents an entirely new way to experience Conflict, and we look forward to seeing the creativity of players on the battlefield.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42399725/4b9b3e7359de489da58c5bb6bf30b1945c87cf8d.jpg"]
In addition to the base game modes like Game Master and Combat Ops being added to Kolguyev, players will also be able to enjoy some solo content as we introduce two new singleplayer experiences:
Operation Omega – a five-episode campaign that drops you behind enemy lines, as part of a special forces team operating on Kolguyev.
Air Support – a scenario focused on testing your piloting skills as you’re tasked with a variety of transport, fire support, and logistical missions.
Whether you take to the skies or march through the mud, these missions bring back the cinematic, story-focused gameplay Arma fans have been missing.

The armory has been expanded with new gear and firepower, including new rocket types for the RPG-7, two rocket launchers (RPG-22 and RPG-75), and added camouflage, wrapped versions of the M21 and ART-II. Hand-fired flares are now available to light up the night and mark positions. On the clothing side, players can equip added camouflage patterns such as US Army Tiger Stripe and USSR TTsKO, along with some clothing items of Soviet naval infantry uniforms.

Self-titled combat engineers will find new ways to shape the battlefield with constructable sandbags, mortars, and static weapons that can be carried and deployed almost anywhere. Anti-personnel mines, including the M14 and PMN-4, can also be used to create deadly chokepoints against enemy infantry (and the occasional, absentminded friendly).
Update 1.6 introduces numerous improvements to gameplay systems and core mechanics, which would be too lengthy to list in this article. Here are some quick key features worth mentioning:
FIA Rework - The FIA now features new units, better weapon loadouts, and even civilian fighters.
Moving on Vehicles - Climb onto the back of a flatbed truck and fire while riding along.

HOTAS & Peripheral Support - Preset profiles for HOTAS setups are now included, with customization options planned for the future. Also, Logitech peripherals are fully supported, featuring unique reactive lighting effects for mice and keyboards that respond to in-game events.
Environmental Factors - Foliage now reacts to character movement, and wind affects projectiles like bullets, rockets, and mortars.
Field Manual Expansion - Dozens of new pages have been added to the Field Manual to help you understand the new systems.
Performance Improvements - Hundreds of bug fixes, tweaks, and performance optimizations...
You can read the full 1.6 Update changelog here: Changelog 1.6.0.54

items.text: The game-changing 1.3 update for Arma Reforger brings many new and exciting vehicles, weapons, systems, and improvements. Nowhere on the battlefield is safe anymore and everyone will need to adapt to stay in the fight!

Two new infantry fighting vehicles have reached Everon and Arland. The US forces have gained the LAV-25, with its powerful 25mm M242 autocannon, capable of firing high-explosive rounds and its 7.62mm M240 coaxial machine gun. Both weapons utilize powerful 7x optical sight for target acquisition at long ranges.

The Soviet army and the FIA have been reinforced by the BRDM-2 combat reconnaissance vehicle. It is smaller and lighter than the already-available BTR-70 but equipped with the same firepower: a 14.5mm KPVT machine gun and a 7.62mm PKT.

Command the skies and the pilot seat of the gunship variants of the Mi-8 and UH-1H helicopters. With new fully adjustable collimator sights, detachable rocket pods, and various ammunition options for each gunship, you can keep the enemy forces suppressed and constantly retreating. If you're on the ground make sure to watch the skies and have your RPGs ready!

Arma Reforger brings realistic and immersive mortars into the game! Delay enemy advances, cut off supply routes, level towns, support friendly attacking forces from kilometers away. Both the Soviet 2B14 82mm mortar launcher and its US M252 81mm counterpart change the landscape of the battlefield significantly. Coordinate with spotters near the target area for maximum effect!

Solid cover is now temporary, destruction changes everything! The battlefield will never be the same after a long and intense battle with mortar barrages, helicopter rocket sorties, and vehicular combat. Buildings can be destroyed, entire forests can be cleared, sightlines can be expanded, and chokepoints can be bypassed. Learn to navigate the destructible countryside of Arland and Everon and use it to your advantage.

A brand new singleplayer scenario makes you a US Special Forces soldier tasked with eliminating a high-ranking Soviet officer in the southern town of Régina near the Western Heights. Are you going to take him out from afar with the M21 SWS, prepare an explosive ambush for his UAZ-469, or sneak into town with a suppressed M16 and dispatch the target from up close? The choice is yours!
Supply runs are considerably more effective now that both the M923A1 and the URAL-4320 transport trucks now carry up to 1,500 supplies in a single load.
The UAZ-452 "Buchanka" now comes in two new variants. A transport variant - capable of carrying 7 people or 2 people and 500 supplies, and a cargo variant capable of carrying 800 supplies.
The Šárka 1203 cargo variant can also carry more supplies in this update.
Both the UH-1H and the Mi-8 helicopters now come in civilian colors.
The FIA motor pool has been expanded with the inclusion of the UAZ-452, the BTR-70, and the BRDM-2.

One of the most requested features is the rank requirement system for the Ammunition Supply Depots to address often-disliked "arsenal spam." Players will now have to tangibly contribute to the platoon's efforts and rank up to be able to equip more advanced more expensive weapons and items.
The Conflict game mode has also undergone some significant changes:

Players are now unable to spawn on contested bases.: Previously, capture timers used to rely on the amount of compositions built on each base. In 1.3, capture time is related to the number of bases connected to the contested one via radio network.: These changes are intended to make the frontlines more dynamic, and will require tactical and strategic adaptation on all sides.
Smaller Conflict game modes are being introduced to give players the option to engage in more condensed and faster-paced battles with the core mechanics of Conflict.

Adjustments to the AI soldiers have made them deadlier than ever! AI are now able to better target moving targets, so simply driving through their roadblocks hoping for the best is not a safe bet anymore. Moreover, once under fire, they seek cover more effectively, return fire aggressively, counterattack, and flank.

Arma Reforger version 1.2.1 brings long-awaited features from the roadmap and other improvements, quality-of-life tweaks, and more.

Soviet and US factions can now equip suppressors to their main assault rifles. The AK-74 and the AKS-74U can now equip the PBS-4 while the M16 and the M16 Carbine use the Mark 3 suppressor. The reduced sound of your weapon and the masked muzzle flash can significantly help to conceal your position from the enemy.
The maximum distance at which grass stops rendering has been doubled from 150 meters to 300 allowing for increased visual fidelity and more engaging combat at a distance.
No more repeated refreshing of the server browser! Join a queue and simply let the game connect you to the server when a space opens up.

Weight matters! Keep an eye on the amount of equipment and ammo in your loadout as overencumbrance now affects your speed and sprinting capabilities. Capturing enemy bases has been improved with the ability to dismantle services. When you are actively capturing, you can now take down enemy services, such as the antenna, which will prevent the enemy from spawning near you. Now, you can also change flashlight colors to prevent the enemy from detecting you at night while still being able to see close by.

Reinforcements have arrived! Just when you thought the frontline was reaching a stalemate, the Arma Reforger 1.2: Reinforcements update brings a host of new assets, features, and improvements that will assist you in your battlefield combat readiness.
From AI commanding and driving to defensive helicopter weapons, flares, bayonets, and more, find out what's new in the new 1.2 Major Update below.

Until now, only humans could operate ground vehicles in Arma Reforger. AI soldiers can now drive, navigate road networks, and avoid obstacles, opening up a world of possibilities for both cooperative and competitive gameplay. AI can also lay down suppressive fire with vehicle weapons, decide which crew member should man the weapons, and reassign a different crew member if the gunner is down.

Take command of your fellow soldiers! Now, you can direct AI comrades to move to different waypoints, halt, lay down suppressive fire, heal one another, follow the squad leader, defend objectives, and get in and out of vehicles. These fundamental commands will allow you to utilize AI soldiers as weapons on the battlefield and more effectively carry out operations across the islands of Everon and Arland. Learn more about our implementation of AI commanding in our latest Dev Report.

Transport helicopters in Arma Reforger have been somewhat vulnerable since 1.0, especially when landing. We've installed mounted weapon turrets on the UH-1H and Mi-8MT to lay down suppressive fire and protect themselves against enemies. This upgrade is sure to change the dynamics of the battlefield, as helicopters are no longer just RPG fodder but a formidable threat to infantry and vehicles alike.
This update introduces three key combat assets that will completely augment nighttime combat, battlefield sabotage, and close-quarters combat:

Flares - Until now, the cover of night has been all-encompassing, with no effective way to increase visibility without significantly compromising your position. We've added underbarrel grenade-launched flares to the game allowing you to tactically illuminate wherever you fire them.

Explosive charges - The US and Soviet factions have both gotten their own explosive charges with detonators, opening up possibilities for sabotage, ambushes, and other explosive tactics on the battlefield. With both timed fuses and detonators, explosive charges will surely shake up engagements across the islands of Everon and Arland.

Bayonets - With attachable bayonets for all three factions, close-quarters combat has become even more deadly. Silently attack with an element of surprise or defend yourself against attackers in close proximity when the fight comes to you.

The Soviet arsenal has gotten another weapon! Introducing the AKS-74U - a lightweight, shortened variant of the AK-74 well suited for close-quarters combat. It's the perfect complement for an AT or medic loadout, allowing soldiers to specialize in their roles without compromising firepower.

In addition, new pilot suits and gloves expand your options for authentic kits for in-game factions, reinforced by multiple new soldier roles, including US and Soviet special forces units placeable by the Game Master.
Two of the most requested waypoint features for Game Master are now in-game!

Cycle waypoints allow you to make cyclical routes for AI soldiers. Previously, AI could just be sent from point A to B. With cycle waypoints, you can loop their patrol route indefinitely, making it easier for a Game Master to set up a scenario and create a more immersive environment for the players.

Linking waypoints allow you to link waypoints with entities. For example, you can now make a waypoint that tells AI to enter a particular vehicle or destroy a specific object. This added level of control will give you more options for creating scenarios and leading thrilling Game Master sessions on the fly.

And finally, the civilian faction is now available in Game Master mode. You can now utilize civilians in your operations and spawn them with randomized loadouts with percentage chance values for which gear they will receive.

The inventory has received a massive overhaul, greatly improving functionality and performance. Inventory replication has been refactored, addressing performance issues caused by the previous system. Drag-and-drop has been improved, and the entire inventory UX/UI has received a cosmetic overhaul. We think the new inventory is a significant upgrade and hope you enjoy the new interface!

Next time you're engaging an FIA squad, you'll probably notice that AI soldiers can more accurately suppress your position thanks to our updated AI firing behaviors! In addition to suppressive fire being an AI command, AI will use suppressive fire to cover and suppress an area with both bullets and indirect fire grenades. They will also more quickly suppress suspected enemy positions if attacked and will do so for longer.
In addition, firing timing logic has been completely redone to achieve more natural firing patterns and allow the AI to better regulate the firing rate during different combat situations.

Deployable radios have gone through several iterations already, and the latest version brings more to the table than ever before. Now, deployable radios can be refilled with supplies and use supplies in their immediate vicinity. Instead of abandoning a deployed radio that has run out of spawns, you can refill it with supplies to enable more spawns. This also means that radios cost 200 supplies, as they come loaded with 100 supplies worth of spawns. In addition, Game Masters have the option to switch between three different types of budgets for radios (unlimited spawning, supply usage, and limited spawn tickets), and a new use action visible to the owner of the radio allows for spawning with loadouts to be disabled.
Finally, we have three new features that address issues identified by our community:

Vehicle unflipping is now in-game, so you can get out of a bind more easily if you accidentally overturn your vehicle. However, be aware that the feature often requires teamwork, just as it would in the real world.
Copilots can now take over the controls of a helicopter if the pilot is incapacitated.

The "get-in/get-out" refactor addresses several issues with vehicles. Now, opening the door and getting into a vehicle are two separate actions. This means no more repeatedly opening and closing helicopter doors; now, you can get in or out of any vehicle while leaving the door open. As a part of this factor, vehicles without roofs that go careening through the air and flip over can also eject passengers, and passengers exiting vehicles traveling at speed can be seriously injured by doing so.
We hope you enjoy the latest update to Arma Reforger. Please read the full changelog for a detailed breakdown of all the new additions, changes, and tweaks.

In a bold departure from conventional military simulation, we invite players to step into a world where the green and red armies clash in an imaginative battlefield straight out of your childhood dreams.

Tiny Wars is a testament to our commitment to innovation and creativity. Never before has any gaming franchise so effectively paired military simulator gameplay with meticulously recreated retro miniatures.
Micro Soldiers - Lead your army of bullet-sized warriors into battle
Whimsical Environments - Immerse yourself in a larger-than-life landscape that brings the toy box to life
No Choking Hazard - All of the immersive warfare of years past with none of the pesky plastic danger
So gear up and unleash your inner child as you take the fight to the world of Tiny Wars: The Micro Military Simulator!
Play now and engage in tactical living room warfare today!

We're proud to release the Arma Reforger 1.1 Update: Resistance Ops. This major update introduces new playable content, civilian clothing, weapons and optics, vehicles, and more. It also includes a multitude of fixes and improvements. Players can now play as the guerilla resistance faction and collaborate together to liberate the island in a new cooperative scenario.
On the island of Everon, the local resistance has been beaten into submission by the invading Soviet forces - but they will not accept defeat sitting down.

In this game mode, join the FIA and collaborate with up to 5 friends to liberate the island of Everon. Players can battle it out against improved AI in a dynamic scenario that offers a different experience every time. Raid camps, destroy objectives, seize arms, and break the enemy's stranglehold on the island.

All three factions have received new weapons, reworked models, and upgraded weapon variants. Introducing the all-new US M16A2 Carbine, enhanced optics for both US and Soviet factions, and an expanded arsenal for the FIA, which now includes the UK-59L machine gun, NSV turret, and even an armed UAZ.

The FIA now has a selection of civilian clothing to help conceal themselves and build their guerilla resistance. Join their cause and cruise around the islands in style with the Šárka S1203 and S105, two civilian vehicles based on popular Czech automobiles from the 80's.

This update has introduced two crucial improvements to AI behavior making non-human players more formidable adversaries on the battlefield. They now demonstrate improved tactics like seeking cover from fire and employing smoke grenades when aiding downed comrades. These new behaviors are very noticeable in-game, and we think you will find your AI opponents (and teammates) to be much more effective combatants.

Lighting both indoors and out has been significantly improved. Overall, the lighting is more vibrant, which is especially noticeable during the picturesque sunrises and sunsets of Arland and Everon. New clouds with more authentic and variable shapes cast more explicit shadows in cloudy weather. In addition, the lighting coming into buildings from the outside is more explicit, and foliage obstructs sunlight much more naturally, even from a distance.
A plethora of new fixes, tweaks, and enhancements have been integrated. Below are some key improvements aimed at boosting your gameplay experience:
Radios must now be deployed to spawn on them — This limitation requires you to deploy radio backpacks to prepare for offensive maneuvers strategically.

Fast travel is now limited to deployed radios — While it used to be fun to teleport across the map at will, the previous implementation of fast travel detracted from the game's realism and immersion. Now, strategically deploying radios is crucial.

Living quarters can only spawn a set number of AI — "Living quarter spam" is no longer an issue as the number of AI per base is now limited. Not to mention, spawning AI costs a decent amount of supplies.

Spawning at bases under attack takes longer — Defenders can no longer quickly and repeatedly spawn into a base being captured, which previously gave them an unfair advantage and made capturing bases extremely difficult.

Supplies spawn more slowly and are capped at lower amounts in bases — Logistics is more important than ever, and if your team isn't running supplies, you will find it even more difficult to gain an advantage and hold your points.
We hope you enjoy the latest update to Arma Reforger. Please read the full changelog for a detailed breakdown of all the new additions, changes, and tweaks.

As we approach the upcoming 1.0 version of Arma Reforger, we must inform you of some changes that will impact modders but are necessary to provide the best experience for everyone moving forward.

More specifically, there are many changes in the update that will impact currently published mods. The differences in the approaching release make it impossible to know if every Workshop mod has been updated to be compatible with the latest build. Unfortunately, it’s not within our capacity to fix or check every mod currently available in the Workshop. We know that a significant number of released mods will be incompatible with this update, and thus, crashes will be introduced for players using these mods. This could potentially result in consequences for the game as a whole.

After much consideration, we have decided that temporarily delisting all mods in the Workshop is the best course of action. Do not worry, though! None of your mods will be erased, and mod creators won’t lose any data or access to your mods. Mods (including mod dependencies) will be hidden and marked as incompatible for 1.0 if they have not been published with the latest Arma Reforger Tools version yet. Delisted mods will be usable only in single player and workbench, but hosting of servers with outdated mods won't be possible with the latest version of Arma Reforger.
To restore your mod to the Workshop, you’ll need to follow the process below:
On November 13, 2023, all public mods on the experimental environment will be marked incompatible and hidden from the Workshop.
On November 16, 2023, all public mods on all environments will be marked incompatible and hidden from the Workshop.
We strongly advise each mod creator to assess their compatibility with 1.0 and fix any potential bugs that may arise due to changes in the new version.
Mod creators must manually publish an update for their mods to the Workshop using the Arma Reforger Tools to make them public and available again.

If you discover that your mod is incompatible with 1.0 and need advice on updating it, please reach out on the Arma Discord or Bohemia Interactive Forums, where either our devs or the community can suggest fixes or areas to focus on.

We apologize for this inconvenience. We strongly feel this is the best way to mitigate the risk of old and unmaintained mods negatively impacting the game, and the player experience. We look forward to seeing your updated mods in the workshop and running smoothly in 1.0!
